findings.evidence: All three declarations take a finite-indexed basis. Mathlib provides `Module.Finite.of_basis b` and `Module.Free.of_basis b`, while `Module.Projective.of_free` supplies projectivity; thus callers should not need separate typeclass instances for facts already witnessed by `b`.
findings.fix: Remove the section-level assumptions and construct local `Module.Finite`, `Module.Free`, and hence `Module.Projective` instances from each argument `b : Basis (Fin n) R M` before applying `matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_prod_dual`.
findings.issue: The section assumptions `[Module.Finite R M] [Module.Projective R M]` unnecessarily restrict `coordinateBialgHom_range_eq_matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_prod_dual` and `coordinateBialgHom_surjective_iff_matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_prod_dual`; the same issue recurs for `isFaithful_iff_matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_prod_dual` at line 253.

summary: The three dual-coefficient theorems impose redundant finite/projective typeclass assumptions already supplied by their finite basis argument.
